subject: Cooking
title: Canning: Napoleon's Accidental Food Revolution
description: One-minute skill: Canning: Napoleon's Accidental Food Revolution.

hook.text: Napoleon offered 12,000 francs to anyone who could keep food fresh for his armies. A confectioner won.

buildup.text: Nicolas Appert discovered that sealing food in airtight jars and boiling them prevented spoilage.

discovery.text: Appert didn't know why it worked — Pasteur wouldn't explain microbes for another 50 years.

twist.text: Early tin cans used lead solder. The Franklin expedition likely died from lead poisoning from their canned food.

climax.text: Modern canning is one of the safest preservation methods — billions of cans are consumed safely each year.

punchline.text: A war prize became the world's pantry.

quiz.question: Who first developed the canning preservation method?

details.summary: Nicholas Appert invented canning in 1810 to preserve food for Napoleon's armies, sealing food in jars and heating them to sterilize the contents. He did not know why it worked — Pasteur explained bacterial death decades later.
details.whyItMatters: Canning made safe, long-term food storage possible for the first time in history. It transformed military logistics, global food trade, and household food security.
takeaways: Heat sterilization inside sealed containers preserves food for years
Pressure canning reaches 240°F needed to kill botulism spores
Acid foods like tomatoes can be safely water-bath canned

faq.question: Why do low-acid foods require pressure canning?
faq.answer: Botulism spores survive boiling water at 212°F. Pressure canners raise the temperature to 240°F, which is lethal to the spores. Low-acid foods like vegetables, meat, and beans must reach this temperature. High-acid foods below pH 4.6 prevent botulism growth without pressure.

faq.question: How long do canned foods actually last?
faq.answer: Properly sealed canned food remains safe almost indefinitely because the sterile, sealed environment prevents bacterial growth. However, quality declines over time. Most manufacturers recommend one to five years for best taste and nutrition. Decades-old canned food has been found safe to eat.
